evidence.quote: yields improved $\alpha$ Cen A and B orbital elements, system proper motion and parallax, and component masses.

claims.hypothesis: alpha Cen AB and Proxima form a bound system
claims.experiment: compared differential space velocity with the unbound velocity limit
claims.result: 280 +/- 32 m/s vs limit 554 +/- 7 m/s; significance 8.3 sigma
claims.finding: the three stars constitute a bound system

evidence.quote: confirms that the three stars constitute a bound system

claims.hypothesis: continued ALMA astrometry can detect planets in the stable region around A and B
claims.experiment: noise-floor estimate from a hypothetical 20-epoch campaign with 100-500 microarcsec per-epoch precision
claims.result: noise floor about 55 microarcsec, enough for a 25 Earth-mass planet at 2 AU
claims.finding: sensitivity to planets of a few 10s of Earth masses at 1-3 AU is expected, not yet demonstrated

evidence.quote: we will ultimately be sensitive to planets of a few 10s of Earth mass in orbits from 1-3 AU

why_this_data.value: Band 7 chosen to balance SNR, angular resolution and field of view for 10-100 mJy stars at 2-21 arcsec separation

evidence.quote: From these parameters and looking to balance the SNR, the angular resolution and the field of view, we selected to observe in band 7.

why_this_method.value: astrometric precision scales with angular resolution, so long baselines are preferred

evidence.quote: As the astrometric precision scales directly with the angular resolution, observations when ALMA is in configurations with maximum baselines of 2 km or larger are most desirable

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: RVs from CES and UVES rejected because zero-point shifts add fit variables and degrade reliability

evidence.quote: We tested incorporating additional radial velocity measurements from other spectrographs (in particular CES and UVES).
